Hi all — I pulled the ledger export and dug into the per-entity proration. Summary first, details below and attached CSV (proration-ledger-mercator-may2027.csv):

Summary:
- Root cause: per-entity rounding policy. We prorate the hosted charge at 8 decimal precision, then round to the invoice currency (EUR) per-entity before VAT is applied.
- When the proration splits a charge across entities that have different VAT treatment flags, rounding to cents per entity can create small residuals compared to applying VAT on the aggregated amount. For MercatorAI this produced a net +0.03 EUR VAT on the two entity lines vs aggregated VAT on the full amount.
- Actions: propose issuing a corrective credit of 0.03 EUR to MercatorAI and adjusting the May ledger to mark the rounding residual as a manual rounding-correction GL entry.

Reconciliation excerpt (simplified):
Base hosted charge (grossable): 1,234.567891 EUR
Prorated to EU-A: 617.2839455 -> rounded to 617.28 EUR -> VAT @21% = 129.63 EUR
Prorated to EU-B: 617.2839455 -> rounded to 617.29 EUR -> VAT @21% = 129.63 EUR

If you instead aggregate then apply VAT:
Total base rounded: 1,234.57 EUR -> VAT @21% = 259.26 EUR
Sum of per-entity VAT above = 259.29 EUR -> delta = +0.03 EUR

Attached CSV includes the full per-entity steps, currency rounding function used (Bankers rounding to 2 decimals), and GL codes. The customer is correct that this is a rounding artifact introduced by per-entity invoice construction.

Next steps recommended:
1) Issue a 0.03 EUR credit note (proposed-credit-note-0_03EUR.pdf) and apply to the May invoice balance.
2) Create a short internal KB describing the rounding edge and a flag to toggle aggregated VAT calculation for multi-entity customers with mixed VAT flags.
3) Confirm with TaxOps whether a VAT correction note is needed for EU reporting — Neha, can you advise?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference

Hi Lars / team — thanks for raising this and thanks Ben for the analysis. I've reviewed the ledger export Ben attached and consulted with our EU tax counsel.

Short answer: the 0.03 EUR is a non-substantive rounding residual and can be remedied with a credit note. For VAT reporting: because the underlying taxable base and VAT rate were correctly applied per entity, a corrective credit is acceptable; no additional VAT re-invoicing is required from our side if the customer accepts the credit. We'll issue a credit note referencing the original invoice number and include the per-entity proration CSV for audit.

Resolution steps we've completed / scheduled:
- Issued provisional credit note: 0.03 EUR (proposed-credit-note-0_03EUR.pdf attached).
- Adjusted internal ledger with GL reversal for the rounding residual (code GL-RND-ADJ).
- Created HubSpot ticket for tracking and compliance: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/MT-98765 (attached to the customer record).
- KB task opened to add an account-level option: "aggregate-vat-for-multi-entity" to avoid future cent-level deltas for customers that prefer aggregated VAT.

Lars — if MercatorAI agrees to the modest credit, we'll finalize and post the corrected invoice and update the tax note in the customer portal. Please confirm and we'll proceed.

Best,
